summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) focused on performance optimization across CPU and GPU architectures. Hand-wrote custom CUDA C++ kernels with memory coalescing for measurable inference speedups and built MPI-distributed workloads on SLURM clusters with load-balancing and scaling analysis. Comfortable in C/C++ across x86, ARM, and Jetson-class SoC targets, with latency profiling and benchmarking throughout.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Designed a custom wavelet bank (alpha-blended sym6+bior3.5) combined with optimized homography stitching and concurrency to reach a PSNR of 86 over a baseline PSNR of 65.
Deployed ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation for crack-depth profiling with +/-8% error, integrated into a full metal-surface inspection pipeline.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Engineered a data pipeline for the BraTS 2020 MRI dataset with batch-loading memory management for large 3D volumetric inputs; reported accuracy-latency trade-offs across VGG-16/19 and ResNet-50 U-Net backbones.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript conv layers in VGG16 with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights/biases, and preallocated global buffers to eliminate per-layer allocation overhead.
Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms vs 73.3ms uncoalesced and 77.5ms CPU TorchScript, a ~35% speedup over naive GPU with 1.5-2x faster convolutions at identical accuracy.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Implemented and benchmarked four parallel work-distribution strategies (static strip/block/cyclic, dynamic task queue) for rendering 5000x5000 pixel scenes using MPI.
Achieved up to 30x speedup with static strip partitioning (55 processes); dynamic task queue outperformed all static methods under unpredictable workloads.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place system over a three-layer distributed pipeline (Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, Jetson+Arduino controller) on a unified WebSocket fabric.
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO for visual servoing at 5.2x speedup (56.7 to 10.9 ms vs eager PyTorch); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10) at ~11.5s end-to-end latency.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Reduced GPU memory footprint ~55% via 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) on TinyLlama 1.1B; profiled peak VRAM and inference latency across prompt types using pynvml and psutil.

awards: Ranked 10th, Robocon - National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
